Rinku finishes it off in style and quickly at that! Tossed up full on middle and leg, he 
gets under it and sends it high and long over deep backward square leg. KKR win big 
with eight wickets and 59 balls to spare 
Sunil Narine, Player of the Match: "Almost [a complete game], next time hope I can take 
a catch as well. Try to focus on my strength. Batters play well but if you focus too much 
on batters, you are already on the back foot. You get accustomed and try to adapt as 
soon as possible. You see what happens in the powerplay and try and help the team. It's 
very simple - trying to get the team off to a flying start. Sometimes it works, sometimes 
it doesn't." 
Ajinkya Rahane, KKR captain: "We played here last two years - Moeen played here, DJ 
knows the conditions. We didn't think it would be too sticky and that our spinners will 
get help. We had our plans and that worked well for us tonight. Still long way to go in the 
tournament, I don't want to share too many things. In the end, it looks spot on. Initially I 
thought it was a 170-180 wicket. Moeen set us up, tough for him to play and then miss 
out. Sunny and Varun dominated the middle overs for us. Really happy with Vaibhav and 
Harshit, the way they came and executed the plans. I am enjoying my batting, worked 
hard last two-three years. It is about staying in the moment than thinking too ahead. 
First it was about taking two points, after six overs, we thought if we finish it early, it will 
help us. Sometimes you play good cricket, you lose as well. Last game we lost by four, it 
was about starting from scratch. Boys are preparing well, there is positive intent." 
Moeen Ali: "Having two left-handers helped my case. Kept as straight as possible. Rinku 
dived and stopped four early, that helped my confidence. In powerplay, you cannot bowl 
quick. Give it time to spin. Sometimes it skids on, sometimes it spins. Sunil has been 
outstanding for a long time. If I can bowl a couple of overs at the top and save them for 
later, helps. I am learning from them. At the top you can't spin every ball. You just need 
one to grip and that puts doubts in the batters' minds." 
MS Dhoni, CSK captain: "Quite a few nights haven't gone our way. Need to look deep 
down inside. Challenge was there, but we needed to tackle. Didn't have enough runs on 
the board today. Ball stopped that has been the case, even in the second innings it 
stopped. Today it stopped in the first innings as well. With quality spinners, it is difficult. 
We didn't get partnerships as well. [Powerplay batting] It is important to see the 
conditions. A couple of conditions where we have done well. We don't want to match 
somebody else or some other team. We have quality openers and it is important not to 
get desperate seeing the scoreboard. A few boundaries and the score keeps moving, if 
we target 60, it gets tough. If we lose wickets, the middle order needs do heavy-lifting 
and the slog never comes." 
This is the biggest margin of defeat for CSK in the IPL in terms of balls remaining. 
At the innings break, Rana spoke about how change-ups were making the ball grip the 
surface. But we saw Khaleel and Kamboj both go for pace and they travelled. With not 
much pressure, CSK's spinners weren't spared either but Noor did make a small mark 
on the game. Lots to ponder for the five-time champs. 
10:27pm A massive thrashing for CSK and they lose five games in a row for the first 
time in the IPL. This is also their third consecutive defeat at Chepauk, another first. 
Nothing really went right for CSK tonight. Narine got KKR off to a flier before Rahane 
and Rinku dealt the opposition the final blow. 
An early finish then. Not in the manner you'd expect. The slightly surprising bit is that 
CSK are not at the bottom of the points table despite their biggest defeat. The games 
keep on rolling. Lots of cricket tomorrow, with two games each in the IPL and the PSL. 
Do join us for all of that and more. Till then, on behalf of Chandan and Ashish, this is 
Sudarshanan saying goodnight! Ciao, fellas!
